extractor.note: Grep-searched the whole file for 'immutable', 'vera et immutabilis', 'true and immutable', 'geometry/geometric/geometrical', 'essence of the triangle', 'eidos', 'innate' and 'residuum'; closely read lines 90-149 and 190-319 (chapters II-IV) paragraph by paragraph. Lines 1-89, 150-189 and 320-371 (chapter I's mathesis universalis material and chapter V's Pascal material) were keyword-scanned but not closely read, hence coverage is declared partial.

coverage_note: Covers chapter II §6 (p. 80-82, the Rule XIV figuratum passage) and chapter IV §20 (pp. 276-281, the fifth-Meditation 'true and immutable natures' passage) in full. Chapter I (§§1-5, pp. 1-72), the ego/substance material of chapter III not already read (roughly pp. 160-176), and chapter V (Pascal, pp. 296-324) were only keyword-scanned for the theme's search terms, not read paragraph by paragraph.

units.claim: The idea of God in the fifth Meditation is presented as an innate idea drawn from the same reserve of thought as every other innate idea, not from experience.
units.quote: exactly as all the innate ideas are drawn from thought, the idea of God is drawn from the reserve where, among others, it was as it were stocked

units.claim: Innate ideas are said to offer their true and immutable natures, each attesting a determinate nature, essence or form of it, immutable and eternal.
units.quote: namely all those that offer their true and immutable natures and so attest a certain determinate nature or essence or form of it, immutable and eternal

units.claim: Marion states that the idea of God is found in the mind no less than the idea of a triangle, placing it among the simple natures of extension, figure and number.
units.quote: the idea of God is found in me no less, that is, at most as much, as the idea of a triangle, and so as the simple natures of extension, figure, number

units.claim: Because determination [B], God as supremely perfect, shares the epistemic status of the true-and-immutable simple natures, Marion concludes it contradicts determination [A], God as incomprehensible infinite.
units.quote: it must definitively be admitted that [A] and [B] contradict one another on the parameter of incomprehensibility

absences.expected_because: This passage treats an extended geometrical figure at length as an object the mind reduces to a minimal ens (Rule XIV's figuratum: body, surface, line, point) - the same kind of geometrical object that section 20 later calls a true and immutable nature - yet describes it only as an ens 'respectu intellectus nostri', without the immutable-nature vocabulary.
absences.note: The passage uses essentia and figure extensively but never pairs geometrical figure with immutable-nature vocabulary; that pairing appears only later, at section 20, once Marion turns to the fifth Meditation.
